title: Reconstruct a real nearest-neighbour Hamiltonian from one complex response
statement: For N>=2, nonzero s_j=Im(conj(y_j)*y_(j+1)) for all edges and sum_j Im(conj(y_j)*z_j)=0 give a unique real symmetric tridiagonal H with Hy=z. Set J_j=[sum_(k=1)^j Im(conj(y_k)*z_k)]/s_j, with absent boundary hoppings zero; set epsilon_j=Re(conj(y_j)*(z_j-J_(j-1)*y_(j-1)-J_j*y_(j+1)))/|y_j|^2.

requires: Supplied length-N complex y,z, finite N>=2; one design energy and a real symmetric nearest-neighbour matrix class.
Every adjacent s_j nonzero and global Im<y,z>=0; evaluate the full reconstruction at the declared arithmetic precision.
provides: For N>=2, nonzero s_j=Im(conj(y_j)*y_(j+1)) for all edges and sum_j Im(conj(y_j)*z_j)=0 give a unique real symmetric tridiagonal H with Hy=z. Set J_j=[sum_(k=1)^j Im(conj(y_k)*z_k)]/s_j, with absent boundary hoppings zero; set epsilon_j=Re(conj(y_j)*(z_j-J_(j-1)*y_(j-1)-J_j*y_(j+1)))/|y_j|^2.
assumptions: No simultaneous multi-input, derivative/band, positive-energy/Schur, Maxwell or finite-time guarantee follows.
Zero-current edges need a separate existence/nonuniqueness analysis; small denominators can make control magnitudes/precision unbounded.
costs: N site controls and N-1 real hoppings plus target acquisition, precision, conditioning and complete bath/physical calibration.
Linear prefix arithmetic once y,z are supplied is not an end-to-end physical construction cost bound.
contract.units: y is an excitation amplitude vector; z has energy times amplitude units. s_j has amplitude-squared units; J_j and diagonal epsilon_j have energy units with hbar=1. N counts sites; B is the source energy scale. State norm errors and numerical residuals are not probabilities or device yield.
contract.obstruction: Acquire and test one common calibrated positive full response over every required input and energy before transferring this local algebra to a gate.

body: For each row, real diagonal contributes no imaginary product. Writing t_j=Im(conj(y_j)*z_j) gives t_j=-J_(j-1)*s_(j-1)+J_j*s_j. Prefix sums force the displayed J; the zero global sum closes the last row. Every y_j is nonzero because all adjacent s are nonzero, and the residual divided by y_j is real, giving the displayed epsilon. These forced coefficients also prove uniqueness. This is one supplied response at one design energy; it is not a common multiport or band synthesis theorem. Exact curator diagnostic: y=(1,i),z=(i,1) forces H1=[[0,1],[1,0]], whereas y=(1,2i),z=(4i,2) forces H2=[[0,2],[2,0]]. Each is legal alone; no one matrix satisfies both. A conditioning/positivity diagnostic uses y=(1,1+i*d),z=(i,-i),d>0: J=1/d and both diagonals=-1/d, with eigenvalues0,-2/d. Bounded target vectors can thus force arbitrarily large controls and a negative eigenvalue. These are algebraic interface diagnostics, not actual photon-source calibrations. If s_j=0, the corresponding prefix current must vanish but the quotient is unavailable; real y with imaginary incompatible z can satisfy the global condition and still have no real solution. Read the actual native passage; its 44-site residual and sampled photon errors require unavailable governing arrays/code and are not accepted certificates.

evidence.range_scope: Written single-response Jacobi reconstruction; intake audit reconstructs the row-current proof and missing explicit diagonal formula.
evidence.status: Exact frozen source bytes; scientific acceptance is scoped to actual version-bound review.

review.scope: Completed source-exposed intake-author reconstruction of the finite real-Jacobi response theorem from native lines48–66. Taking imaginary row products gives t_j=-J_(j-1)*s_(j-1)+J_j*s_j; prefix summation fixes every hopping and the global sum enforces the last row. The explicit real diagonal then closes Hy=z and gives uniqueness. Exact Gaussian-rational small-chain recovery, incompatible global/zero-current cases, a simultaneous-response counterexample and an ill-conditioned nonpositive family check these boundaries. The last two are curator algebraic diagnostics, not producer photonic ports or a broad device no-go. No original scientific program, numerical scattering/Schur/TE-grid suite, Maxwell solver, primary-paper audit or physical experiment was executed. Numerical claims remain source reports, and one-body positivity is not a many-body/continuum gap or complete operation.
